newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks end down on Ramos health worries.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks end down on Ramos health worries.

text.p: Manila stocks slumped at the close on Wednesday as false rumours that President Fidel Ramos collapsed on Tuesday revived worries about his health, traders said.
"That rumour (that Ramos collapsed) affected the market. Some said if there's smoke there is fire," said Monique Lecaros, trading supervisor at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
On Tuesday, Ramos denied he was sick and said he was in good health.
The composite index dropped 18.87 points or 0.56 percent to 3,339.83, but was off the day's low of 3,332.04.

Traders said speculative issues such as Pacifica, Sinophil, Atlas Fertiliser, Abacus and Anglo grabbed the limelight from blue chips. "Issues that were supposed to be dead are being resurrected," said Lecaros.
Traders said they expected the market to remain in negative territory for the rest of the week as investors try to shore up liquidity for the upcoming initial public offer.
Upcoming new issues include Equitable Bank and aluminum maker Reynolds Philippine Corp. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-89-36
